transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-25 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Holloway Procurement), Lina (Holloway CISO), Tara (FinOps), Aaron (Legal)

Summary (auto): Quick intake to map redlines and pilot.

-- Transcript --
[00:00:00] Jesse: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Jesse Carter here from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya and I will run through the intake.
[00:00:09] Mark: Hey Jesse, thanks. We have about 50 minutes. I'll let Lina lead on security items, Aaron on legal redlines and Tara on cost approvals.
[00:00:20] Priya: Great, I'll start with a short overview of the deployment options so we can tie the DPA/MSA asks to the right offering — hosted API, dedicated, and private VPC/on-prem.
[00:00:34] Priya: So, high level — hosted is fastest, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, private gives control over networking and KMS. We call the cost tool Redwood Optimize internally, but sometimes the transcript spells it Red wood op- — sorry, typo, but you'll see suggestions for batching/quantization.
[00:00:48] Lina: One thing up front — Holloway will require customer-managed KMS for any PII or payment-related models. We need to know if Redwood Private supports HSM/KMS integrations and whether key material ever leaves the customer's control.
[00:01:03] Priya: Yes, Private supports KMS integrations with common cloud KMS and HSMs. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS but we can discuss an escrow/bring-your-own-key workflow for high-risk data. There's a nuance on logs though — audit logs are generated at the control plane for debugging, we can mask or exclude request payloads on request.
[00:01:22] Aaron: On the MSA/DPA side, our legal team typically pushes for explicit data residency and deletion language plus a carve-out for customer-submitted models. Also, indemnity cap questions and SLA remedy structure — credits vs termination.
[00:01:36] Jesse: Totally. For SLAs we usually include uptime targets for the control plane, and per-request latency P95 targets for Dedicated. We can propose financial credits for missed SLOs and an escalation ladder — for enterprise deals we are open to discussing higher remedies.
[00:01:52] Mark: Also need to understand egress fees. If we replicate models into region X for compliance, what's the recurring cost?
[00:02:01] Priya: Egress depends on the infrastructure. For Dedicated in-region it's minimal; cross-region replication has inter-region transfer. We'll include a sheet with estimated egress scenarios.
[00:02:12] Tara: From FinOps perspective, we need a clear commit vs variable cost model. If we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, what's the discount band and what flexibility do we have for burst capacity?
[00:02:24] Jesse: Good question. We can do a reserved capacity contract with tiered discounting and a burst pool; the commercial term sheet will show commit levels, minimum utilization, and overage rates. We'll propose a 12-month case and a 24-month case for comparison.
[00:02:37] Lina: Security artifacts — SOC 2 Type II, recent pen test, architecture diagram, and an approach to key rotation. If you have a security packet please share.
[00:02:48] Jesse: Yes, we have a security pack and SOC 2 report. Priya will share the pack and a short FAQ about KMS and log retention.
[00:02:56] Priya: Quick demo note — if you go Dedicated you can pin model versions and have canary rollouts. That might be relevant for your change-control teams.
[00:03:10] Aaron: For the DPA, indemnities — we usually accept liability caps but need carveouts for gross negligence. Can you confirm Redwood's standard cap and whether you accept carveouts?
[00:03:20] Jesse: Our standard cap is typically a multiple of fees (one to three x) — but for enterprise deals we can negotiate; carveouts are commonly handled case-by-case. We'll flag the relevant clauses in the MSA and suggest language.
[00:03:33] Mark: Timeline — we need production access before fiscal Q3. Is a three-week pilot feasible to validate latency and integration?
[00:03:43] Priya: Yes, a 2–3 week pilot is typical: baseline tests for latency/throughput, a small workload to test KMS flow, and validations for cache behavior. We'll need dedicated GPU pool access for throughput tests.
[00:03:58] Tara: Will the pilot cost be billable or complimentary?
[00:04:02] Jesse: We usually offer a discounted pilot credit; for enterprise pilots there may be a small fee to cover reserved capacity during the test. We'll outline options.
[00:04:12] [00:04:12] Line noise / crosstalk
[00:04:16] Lina: A couple of detailed questions — audit logging retention windows, and can we get per-tenant log exports to our SIEM?
[00:04:25] Priya: You can export logs to your SIEM via S3/Cloud Storage connectors or a streaming integration; retention windows are configurable but for hosted plans there's a default. For Private we can match your retention policy.
[00:04:39] Aaron: On DPA sub processors — list please. Also need clarity on whether any model editing or fine-tuning by Redwood would be performed; we want assurances our data won't be used to train public models.
[00:04:52] Jesse: Redwood's policy is no training on customer-provided prompts unless explicitly enabled; we'll put that in the DPA. We'll also supply the subprocessor list in the security packet.
[00:05:06] Mark: About the SLA credits: does Redwood do graduated credits (e.g., increasing credit % by downtime tier) or a flat monthly credit?
[00:05:15] Priya: We typically do graduated credits tied to incident severity and downtime windows. We'll draft a proposed table for your legal to review.
[00:05:26] Tara: Can you put together modeled cost scenarios: a) POC on hosted, b) pilot on Dedicated with 2x model replicas, c) production on Private with KMS — including egress and storage?
[00:05:39] Jesse: Yes, Priya will create a spreadsheet with those three scenarios and include utilization assumptions.
[00:05:46] [00:20:00] (jump ahead for brevity in transcript)
[00:20:01] Priya: For the Dedicated benchmark we recommend testing with typical sequence lengths and measuring KV cache hit rates; that'll show cost per completed request. Some customers see 30–50% token cost reduction with prefix caching.
[00:20:18] Lina: Regarding encryption in transit, are there FIPS endpoints or TLS min versions we can require?
[00:20:26] Priya: Yes, we support TLS 1.2/1.3 and can accommodate FIPS endpoints for Private. We'll document the cipher suites.
[00:20:34] Aaron: We'll need an audit window for log retention changes — e.g., 30 days notice before retention decreases. Is that standard?
[00:20:42] Jesse: That's reasonable — we'll propose notice periods in the MSA appendix.
[00:20:48] Mark: A policy question — if we need an on-prem package (air-gapped), what's the onboarding timeline?
[00:20:55] Priya: On-prem is the longest path, typically 8–12 weeks for full packaging, depending on networking and security review. VPC deployments are faster, often 2–4 weeks.
[00:21:07] Tara: For pricing, what's the minimum commit to get enterprise terms? We want to know the thresholds — e.g., $X/month or Y GPU hours.
[00:21:16] Jesse: We'll include two commit bands; historically the threshold for custom SLA/pricing is around mid-six figures ARR, but we'll put concrete numbers in the term sheet for Holloway's expected usage.
[00:21:28] Lina: Anything about data residency? We require that payment data remains in region. Can Redwood guarantee that model inference for payment flows stays in region?
[00:21:39] Priya: Yes, routing policies allow regional pinning. We can pin requests to in-region model replicas and avoid cross-region fallbacks for regulated endpoints. We'll note fallback behavior in the control plane config.
[00:21:54] Aaron: Escrow — do you have an escrow option for keys or for source in case of termination?
[00:21:59] Jesse: We offer various escrow options for customer-managed keys and for critical configuration. Source escrow is more complex; we can discuss a limited maintenance escrow as part of enterprise negotiations.
[00:22:12] Mark: Ok, let's outline the immediate deliverables so legal and procurement can move quickly.
[00:22:18] Jesse: Action items: we'll send MSA/DPA redlines, security packet, pricing scenarios, and propose pilot dates.
[00:22:25] Aaron: If you can put redlines in Word with change tracking that helps. Also include a short cover memo explaining the key negotiation points we should focus on.
[00:22:34] Jesse: Will do.
[00:22:38] Tara: Final question — backups and data deletion guarantees? We need how long backups retain data and how it's purged on termination.
[00:22:46] Priya: Default backup retention is 30 days, configurable. On termination we can offer a retention and deletion schedule that meets your compliance needs; we'll propose firm timings in the DPA.
[00:22:58] Lina: Thanks, this was helpful. We'll aim to review the MSA/DPA internally as soon as you send it.
[00:23:05] Jesse: Great — we'll target the due dates we agreed. Thanks everyone.
[00:23:10] [End of recording — meeting continued with offline scheduling notes]
